footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to Truist: after income tax and $333M attributable to noncontrolling interests. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 53.0% to $20.3B in 2025. Net interest income rose 2.4% to $14.4B and noninterest income was $5.9B, versus −$813M; noninterest expense rose 0.6%, and the provision for credit losses was $1.9B, versus $1.9B.
Net income to Truist rose 11.3% to $5.0B, or $3.82 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 59.4% versus 90.4%. Truist returned $5.2B through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to Truist rose 11.3% to $5.0B.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: Truist Financial Corporation Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
